short: Adds low-frequency power (precedent: Pei 2011, Ikeda 2014) and phase-amplitude coupling (new) to imagined-speech ECoG decoding (M06); CFC effect unshown: 12 of 144 uncorrected tests.
position: The paper changes the neural input of an imagined-speech decoder (M06), adding low-frequency power and phase-amplitude coupling (CFC) to broadband high-frequency activity (BHA) [@proix2022imagined]. Low-frequency power has precedent in 2 of the 5 earlier intracranial imagined-speech decoders (Appendix), one of them uncited here [@ikeda2014neural]. CFC input appears in none of the five (Appendix), but its effect is not shown: 12 of 144 uncorrected per-participant tests passed, close to the 7 expected at 5% (inference), with no test against power (Fig. 7). The test partition (M12) is the usual within-participant cross-validation. The authors concede that binary classification is far from a real BCI (Discussion), yet their reading that imagined speech is "equally well" decoded from low and cross-frequency features (Introduction) rests on an imagined BHA baseline with 1 passing pair.
